name: Miguel Díaz-Canel
role: President of Cuba (President of the Council of State 2018-2019, President of the Republic since 2019); First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba since 2021
summary: A Communist Party career official who leads Cuba as head of state and party, defending one-party socialism, state enterprise as the economy's pillar and sovereignty against the US embargo. In office he has opened the economy step by step (currency unification, small and medium private enterprises, foreign and private investment, targeted instead of general subsidies) and backed a progressive Family Code, while his government has jailed protesters and opposition figures and controls the media. In foreign policy he calls for a multipolar order, UN reform, debt relief and aid from rich countries and rejects intervention.

sources.usedFor: National Assembly closing remarks June 2026: reforms said not to contravene the Constitution

universal-healthcare.rationale: Praised Cuba's universal, free health system as a product of the Revolution's social justice and defended it against the pandemic (2021 Assembly speech); the 2019 Constitution makes free health care a state duty (Art. 72).

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In 2026 he said price controls without supply push trade into the informal market and widened private and foreign activity, but kept state conduct of the economy, state enterprise as the main pillar and planning; he rejects neoliberal capitalism (2023, 2021).

public-ownership.rationale: Said the socialist state enterprise remains the fundamental pillar of the economy and strategic sectors stay protected; the Constitution puts key industries and strategic assets under socialist state property (Art. 24). He is opening some activities to private operators, so not stronger.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wants legal security (contracts, usufruct, leases) against arbitrary change for investors, but says land stays 'the people's' and the Constitution gives private property only a complementary role (Art. 22). Mixed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Plans to replace general subsidies with direct support for the vulnerable, guaranteed basket for pensioners and the poor, and says no one will be left alone before the market; he does not call welfare a source of dependency.

central-planning.rationale: Praised China and Vietnam as showing the potential of socialist planning (2021) but in 2026 said central planning should not administer the economy, only set an institutional frame, with plans built from below. Mixed.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Cited the China and Vietnam experiences as references, studied them for the 2026 reform and is widening private, foreign and market channels under Communist Party leadership and state conduct.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Constitution names socialist planning the central component of development (Art. 19); in 2026 he keeps state conduct and protection of strategic sectors by regulation while loosening permissions.

taxation-theft.rationale: Treats tax collection as a duty: pushes electronic invoicing, a creditable VAT and an end to tax evasion in 2026, and says reducing the deficit rests on production and tax revenue.

moral-incentives.rationale: 2026 reform allows variable pay in pesos and foreign currency tied to results, removes salary barriers to keep skilled staff, and he rejects 'igualitarismo'; material incentives are his working method.

collective-farming.rationale: Will hand idle land in usufruct to individual producers, cooperatives and mipymes and give farmers direct access to foreign currency and imports.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Told the UN that capitalism, imperialism and neoliberalism brought colonialism, fascism and apartheid and spread wars and breaches of sovereignty.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said wealth must be created and distributed 'with equity, not with egalitarianism' (2026), while also saying inequalities should shrink until they disappear. Leans against equal outcomes.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: States that the main way to reduce the fiscal deficit is higher production and cutting unnecessary budget spending, and ends general subsidies and price caps.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Announced in 2026 that general price caps will not continue because they failed to contain inflation and caused shortages and a black market; the basket for the vulnerable is kept separately. Recent clear position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Wants social protection 'focalizada y efectiva', replacing general subsidies with direct support to vulnerable people ('subsidiar personas, no productos').

priority-to-poor.rationale: Stated that the first priority before any other is the people who cannot wait for the economy to improve, with targeted programmes in the poorest neighbourhoods.

social-market-economy.rationale: Said reforms mean not leaving anyone alone before the market but to protect better, produce more and regulate intelligently.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Will extend state land in usufruct to producers and said the land 'seguirá siendo del pueblo' and passes to someone else if not productive.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Says land must fulfil its social function or pass to someone who will; the Constitution gives private property a complementary role to socialist state property.

national-resource-control.rationale: Debt-for-asset swaps must not alienate ownership 'in perpetuity'; investment is welcome under sovereign rules; the Constitution reserves natural resources to the state (Art. 11).

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Called for 'selective, intelligent opening' to attract technology, finance, markets and foreign direct investment, direct import and export by firms; rejects isolation.

delink-world-market.rationale: Seeks foreign investment, exports, direct trade and links with Cuban emigrants and foreign firms in 2026, while demanding changes to world economic rules instead of exit from them.

rich-first.rationale: Argues wealth must be created before it can be distributed and rejects egalitarianism, but also says reforms must not widen inequality. Mixed.

capital-controls.rationale: 2026 plan lets firms hold foreign accounts and use foreign-currency payments but only 'bajo regulación estricta' and auditable operations. Mixed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Wants foreign investment widened, including in private firms, while 'protecting strategic sectors by regulation'.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Said waste collection and local services will not be solely state-run and will include foreign, private and community investment, while the state keeps responsibility.

local-production.rationale: Told the Assembly that food production needs attention and each locality's needs be met locally.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Constitution says work is remunerated by quality and quantity as the socialist principle of distribution (Art. 65), but private mipymes are now allowed.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Said the way out is 'Isla adentro' with the least outside dependence, yet he also demands aid and debt relief from rich countries and courts foreign investment.

ban-interest.rationale: Plans to open space to private and foreign financial institutions and new credit mechanisms.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Wants digital payments with traceability, electronic invoicing and auditable cross-border operations to cut evasion and corruption.

independent-unions.rationale: Reported record: only one state-controlled union confederation operates in practice.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Told the Assembly the state has 'a high responsibility it does not renounce' for social justice; also asks firms to sponsor canteens and care homes.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: In 2020 called for eliminating the unpayable external debt of Southern peoples; in 2023, for the G77, called for refinancing and a multilateral renegotiation mechanism rather than outright cancellation (most recent).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Said industrialised countries have the moral duty, historical responsibility and resources to solve global problems and criticised them for missing the 0.7 percent aid target.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Told the G77 'it is for the South to change the rules of the game' and demanded democratising the international financial system; repeated at BRICS 2025.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Described unequal exchange and a financial architecture that exploits and enriches the rich at the expense of the poorest 80 percent.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said a small share of the population holds almost half of world wealth through a system that concentrates riches in a few hands at the majority's expense and is opposed to democratic participation.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Condemned 'irrational patterns of production and consumption' of capitalism as predatory and called opulent societies to change them.

free-trade.rationale: Denounces abusive unequal exchange and rigged trade and financial rules; calls for a new order, not open trade as such.

free-public-college.rationale: Constitution: education is free from preschool to postgraduate level (Art. 73).

defend-planned-state.rationale: Insists the Revolution does not negotiate its existence and that socialism is irrevocable; defended the planned, state-owned system against US pressure in every speech.

one-party-rule.rationale: Said the Party is 'por el carácter de Partido único' the vanguard that should lead, 'the most revolutionary within the Revolution'; Art. 5 makes the Communist Party the superior driving force of state and society.

vanguard-party.rationale: Says the Party must act as the political vanguard and the force that revolutionises the Revolution, with disciplined militants setting an example.

democracy-best.rationale: Defends 'socialist democracy' and says the Party is not an electoral party; the Constitution makes socialism irrevocable (Art. 4) and arrested protesters and dissidents are held (HRW).

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Defines democracy as participation and social justice, not competition between parties, and rules out any change to the socialist system; reported arrests of opposition leaders.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said democracy is more socialist the more participatory it is and called for spaces to take in popular demands; popular consultation held on the Family Code and Constitution.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Cites the 2019 referendum as the people's consent, but no competitive elections are allowed and opponents are prosecuted. Mixed.

direct-votes.rationale: Put the Family Code to a referendum under him (a law of wide reach) but lawmaking otherwise stays with the Assembly.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitution makes the National Assembly the supreme organ (Art. 102) and HRW reports courts subordinate to the executive.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Constitution makes the National Assembly supreme with sole legislative and constituent power (Arts. 102-103); he presents measures to it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The state budget and economic plan go to the National Assembly for evaluation each December.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Holds the presidency while serving as First Secretary of the Communist Party, and speaks in both capacities.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitution makes the president commander in chief and lets him propose the prime minister and ministers to the Assembly (Art. 128).

term-limits.rationale: Constitution (promoted by him) limits the president to two consecutive terms (Art. 126).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Constitution allows only two consecutive presidential terms, binding him as well.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Constitution has the National Assembly elect the president (Art. 126).

recall-officials.rationale: Constitution lets elected representatives be removed at any moment (Art. 101).

recallable-delegates.rationale: Art. 101 of the Constitution says elected representatives may be removed at any moment; practice is limited.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Speaks of the socialist rule of law and said the 2026 measures 'do not contravene the Constitution'.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Names party discipline and collective leadership as permanent topics of Party education.

elective-rulers.rationale: Was chosen president by the Assembly; his succession to Raúl Castro was not hereditary.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Succeeded Raúl Castro, who is not his relative; no relative holds his office.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Calls the Party and mass organisations the channel between leaders and people and the 'most revolutionary' force.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Reported arrests and heavy sentences for protesters and opposition leaders after 11 July 2021, with his call for revolutionaries to take the streets and his talk of prosecuting 'mercenaries'.

party-controls-media.rationale: Constitution makes main media property of the people or political and mass organisations (Art. 55); HRW says the state controls virtually all media.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Denounces US funding of dissidents as subversion, and the 2022 criminal code punishes receiving funds for activities against the constitutional order (HRW).

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Only the Communist Party is allowed and socialism is irrevocable (Arts. 4-5); the main opposition party's leader is imprisoned (HRW).

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Organisations reported countrywide internet outages when the 11 July 2021 protests began; the government did not accept responsibility.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Constitution allows rights to be regulated differently under states of exception (Art. 224).

state-harmful.rationale: Said the state 'has a high responsibility that it does not renounce' and defended the state enterprise and the Party-led state.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Told the Assembly the state has a high responsibility for social justice that it does not renounce; state enterprise stays the pillar.

political-violence-never.rationale: Constitution recognises armed combat against those seeking to topple the order (Art. 4); on 11 July 2021 he called supporters to the streets ('la orden de combate está dada').

revolution-justified.rationale: Celebrates the armed independence wars and the 1959 revolution against a bloody dictatorship, and told the Congress the Revolution would be defended.

leader-cult.rationale: Honours Fidel and Raúl Castro in near-sacred terms ('líder invicto') and mass tributes, yet Cuban law bars statues of Fidel Castro and no personal cult surrounds him. Mixed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Constitution guarantees equality before the law (Art. 42) while HRW reports arbitrary detention of critics. Mixed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Reaffirmed self-determination for Puerto Rico, Western Sahara, Palestine and Cuba itself in his UN speech.

non-intervention.rationale: Rejected intervention in other states' internal affairs by any power, 'sin injerencia externa', and refused foreign 'humanitarian' interference in Cuba.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Called wars of aggression 'disguised as humanitarian interventions' unacceptable and said Cuba does not need humanitarian intervention.

force-without-un.rationale: Condemned force and unilateral action outside the UN Charter (US strike on Iran, 2025).

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Rejects the use of force and aggression and puts defence of the homeland first.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Condemned plans of annexation of territory and 'hegemonism'.

national-mission.rationale: Insists every country has the right to choose its own political system without outside interference.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Condemns colonialism and neocolonialism as the source of Southern underdevelopment.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Called capitalism the origin of colonialism and neocolonialism and demanded an end to them.

colonial-reparations.rationale: At the UN in 2018, 2020 and 2021 backed Caribbean claims for reparations for slavery.

arms-reduction.rationale: Told the UN that 1.74 trillion dollars of military spending is wasted and backed 'general and complete' disarmament.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Stated Cuba ratified the nuclear weapon ban treaty and wants a world without nuclear arms.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Calls for general disarmament and condemned nuclear hegemonism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Cuba ratified the treaty banning nuclear weapons, which also bars hosting them.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Demanded the return of the territory illegally occupied by the US naval base at Guantánamo.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Names preparation for defence a first-order task and cites war-readiness of the whole people.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wants the UN 'revitalised, democratised and strengthened', with a stronger General Assembly and reformed Security Council.

multipolar-world.rationale: Called for a multipolar, democratic and equitable world order.

dominated-front.rationale: Urged the G77 to act together as the South against an unjust order imposed by developed countries.

nation-first.rationale: Defends solidarity and cooperation over narrow interest (Ubuntu), including Cuban medical aid abroad.

defeat-communism.rationale: As First Secretary he defends socialism and communism and calls anti-communist plans an aggression.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Insists socialism is the right path and the only explanation for surviving the siege; blames capitalism for global problems.

close-ties-china.rationale: Praised China's Global Development Initiative and backed the One China principle.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Quoted Fidel against 'universal models' and says each country may choose its political system.

party-own-road.rationale: Says Cuba advances without a proven route, with 'originality', and without foreign tutelage.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Backs a two-state solution on 1967 borders but denounces Israel's 'Zionist regime' and its 'genocide' in Gaza. Mixed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Led the 2022 Family Code campaign, which opened marriage to same-sex couples, saying denying it would deny fundamental rights.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Argued that people of the same sex whose love is hidden by convention deserve legal recognition and protection under the Family Code; the Constitution bars discrimination for sexual orientation.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Family Code defends full equality of women and men; the Constitution says spouses have equal rights (Art. 82).

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Backs full equality between women and men in law (Family Code).

women-suffrage.rationale: Constitution gives men and women the vote at sixteen (Art. 205).

property-franchise.rationale: Constitution grants the vote to all citizens at sixteen (Art. 205).

racial-franchise.rationale: Constitution grants the vote to all citizens regardless of race (Arts. 205, 42).

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Constitution guarantees equality between women and men (Art. 43) and the right of succession (Art. 63).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Heads the government commission behind the national programme against racism and racial discrimination; Constitution bans discrimination by skin colour.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Constitution bans discrimination on many grounds in public services (Art. 42); the anti-racism programme he heads.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Directs the national anti-racism programme, which diagnoses causes and plans actions by territory.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Constitution states Cuba is secular and religious institutions are separate from the state (Art. 15).

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Cuba is a secular republic by its Constitution; Family Code was passed over religious objections.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Constitution says teaching is secular and based on science (Art. 73).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Said believers have every right to defend their conception and the Code protects their type of family; the Constitution guarantees freedom of religion.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Constitution protects the right to change religion (Art. 57).

restrict-conversion.rationale: Constitution protects the right to change one's religion (Art. 57).

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Cuba is secular with equal consideration for all beliefs (Arts. 15, 57).

religious-nation.rationale: Constitution declares the republic secular and religions equal; he stresses religious plurality.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Constitution: sovereignty resides with the people, from whom all state power emanates (Art. 3).

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Constitution: distinct beliefs and religions enjoy equal consideration (Art. 15).

traditional-family.rationale: Told voters the Family Code protects the families religious people defend but equally others, and that denying other family types is exclusion.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Praised the Code for updating and perfecting marriage, de facto union and kinship.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said national unity became possible only by attending to diversity: 'unity in diversity'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said culture is the first thing to save, praised the state's safeguarding of Cuban heritage and ordered a programme of cultural decolonisation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Revolution created systems to protect the national heritage of creators.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Called for assessing art 'without censorship foreign to creation' (2022) but vowed not to allow 'artivists' to desecrate the flag (2021). Mixed.

gradual-change.rationale: 2026 reform plan calls for gradualism and phased pilots, keeping state conduct.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Said cooperation, solidarity and Ubuntu are the only way forward, and blamed capitalism's selfishness.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Blames the egoism and exclusion of capitalism and asks cadres to put 'we before I'.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honoured combatants who fell on 3 January 2026 and the heroes of the nation as examples; closes speeches with 'Patria o Muerte'.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Fuses patriotism with the socialist Revolution and social justice for the people.

patriotic-education.rationale: Constitution says education promotes patriotic values (Art. 73).

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Called for reporting advances in protecting the environment and animals.

future-generations.rationale: Condemned US refusal of the Paris agreement as endangering future generations.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called climate change a question of survival, demanded the opulent countries change production and consumption patterns, and set priority on climate in Cuba.

decide-locally.rationale: Said municipalities must be unleashed with every possible power and plans built from below.

conscription.rationale: Constitution: defence is the supreme duty of every Cuban and the law regulates military service citizens must perform (Arts. 4, 220).

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Puts defence preparation and strengthening the socialist rule-of-law state first under US hostility.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitution condemns imperialism, fascism and colonialism in its foreign policy principles (Art. 16).

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Says Cuba's Assembly is made up of workers and peasants; HRW reports one state-controlled union confederation. Mixed.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Opens waste collection and local services to private and foreign investment while keeping the state responsible.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Says to correct course 'with evidence' but 'without renouncing our firmest principles'.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Constitution grants the right to request true and timely information (Art. 53) while media are state-controlled.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Calls for the integration of Latin America and the Caribbean and unity of Nuestra América.

notes: Where his reforms moved over time the most recent clear position was used (2026 end of general price caps and subsidies; 2023 G77 debt position). Constitution-based answers are medium because the text was drafted under Raúl Castro's lead and approved by referendum; they are used where it records the system he promotes. Cubadebate's 11 July 2021 text is labelled an unofficial version of the address. The Family Code answers rest on state-media reports of his speeches.
